candidates.name: Angiosarcoma
support_spans: Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31
candidates.why: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and cells staining positively with CD31 suggests a vascular tumor, and the clinical presentation is consistent with angiosarcoma.

candidates.name: Kaposi's Sarcoma
support_spans: purpuric patch
centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
candidates.why: The clinical presentation of a purpuric patch with rapid growth and extension is consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma, but the lack of lymphadenopathy and specific histopathological features make it less likely.

candidates.name: Hemangioma
support_spans: irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
candidates.why: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes could suggest a hemangioma, but the rapid growth, central ulceration, and bleeding are not typical features of this condition.

candidates.name: Mycosis Fungoides

candidates.why: The presence of multifocal skin lesions with varying morphology is consistent with mycosis fungoides, a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
